title: Activate genuine nonlocality from distinguishable sets in tripartite systems
authors: Hui-Juan Zuo, Ying-Ying Lu, Shao-Ming Fei
abstract: A set of orthogonal quantum states in multipartite systems is of genuine nonlocality if it is locally indistinguishable in every bipartition. If it is locally reducible when the parties are separated, we say that it has genuine nonlocality of type~\uppercase\expandafter{\romannumeral 1}; otherwise, it has genuine nonlocality of type~\uppercase\expandafter{\romannumeral 2}. For a locally distinguishable set without local redundancy, if there exist some orthogonality preserving local measurements such that each outcome leads to a locally indistinguishable set, then we say that it exhibits the activation of nonlocality. We activate type-\uppercase\expandafter{\romannumeral 1} and type-\uppercase\expandafter{\romannumeral 2} genuine nonlocality of orthogonal product state sets in tripartite systems. In particular, we tackle the local irredundancy problem with partial trace operation and $p$-ary numeral systems to significantly simplify the proofs. Our results also address the open question raised by S. Bandyopadhyay \textit{et al.}[\href{https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevA.104.L050201}{Phys. Rev. A \textbf{104}, L050201 (2021)}]. Furthermore, we observe the activation of hidden genuine nonlocality in multipartite systems, which highlights the applications of nonlocality based on state discrimination in different practical scenarios.
summary: This paper theoretically analyzes how genuine nonlocality can be activated in tripartite quantum systems using sets of orthogonal product states. The authors establish precise conditions and provide explicit constructions for these states, demonstrating the activation of both Type-I and Type-II genuine nonlocality. This advances the understanding of quantum correlations by linking local distinguishability to genuine nonlocality.
main_problem: The paper investigates the conditions under which genuine nonlocality can be activated from a set of quantum states that are initially distinguishable in a tripartite system.
main_result: The authors provide explicit constructions for orthogonal product state sets in tripartite systems that exhibit both Type-I and Type-II genuine nonlocality after applying specific local measurements.
method: The analysis relies on defining genuine nonlocality based on local indistinguishability across all bipartitions, and uses local measurements (OPLMs) to transform distinguishable sets into genuinely nonlocal ones.
model_or_system: The system under study is a tripartite quantum system described by orthogonal product states in the Hilbert space $\text{C}^{d_1} \otimes \text{C}^{d_2} \otimes \text{C}^{d_3}$.
key_observables: Genuine nonlocality (Type I and Type II), local distinguishability, and the existence of orthogonality-preserving local measurements.
important_parameters: The dimensions of the subsystems ($d_1, d_2, d_3$) and the structure of the product states are critical parameters.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the existence of specific local measurements ($K_A, K_C$) capable of activating the nonlocality, and the proofs often rely on specific dimension constraints (e.g., $d_i$ being odd).
figures_summary: The notes reference figures showing distinction details for different parity cases of the dimensions ($d_i$ odd vs. $d_i$ even) in the tripartite system.
paper_structure: The paper builds conceptually by defining genuine nonlocality types, establishing necessary conditions for local indistinguishability (Lemma 1), and then constructing specific sets of states (Propositions 1 & 2) that demonstrate the activation of both Type-I and Type-II genuine nonlocality through local measurements.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous mathematical tools to characterize and generate genuine nonlocality in multipartite systems using product states, which is fundamental for understanding quantum correlations beyond simple entanglement measures.
